key_insight: SIMMER shows that LLM plans can look valid at execution time yet still contain hidden latent failures that silently derail task success or cause irreversible harm.
engineering_relevance: For autonomous household agents, evaluation must go beyond immediate execution errors and check world-state consistency, hazards, and irreversible side effects before deployment.
method: Built a human-curated symbolic kitchen world model with 77 actions, 262 objects, and ~46,800 realistic interactions.
Used a state-machine executor to validate plans against preconditions and detect immediate violations, latent hazards, and irreversible failures.
Tested counterfactual foresight simulation to add explicit state reasoning and reduce hidden failures.
evidence_signal: Across six LLMs, frontier models achieved at most 17% error-free plans, while up to 56% of plans had latent failures and most of those led to irreversible consequences.
watch_item: A symbolic kitchen world model may not capture the full ambiguity, sensor noise, and open-ended dynamics of real homes, so real-world transfer should be validated carefully.
paper_title: SIMMER: Benchmarking Latent Failures in LLM Executable Planning with a World Model
